Date: 2027-02-20T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Preliminary triage: error-rate & cache eviction correlation

Quick update from triage notes (initial):

- Symptom window: 2027-02-18 18:18:47 -> 18:56:12 PST (matches Lighthouse snapshot).
- Error profile: ~7.8% 500-level errors, ~3.2% client timeouts.
- Observed: heavy KV cache churn on the model-serving nodes; consistent small spike in sequence length (median->p95 shift) that increased memory pressure.
- Bottleneck: autoscaler did not bring additional reserved machines fast enough because the workload exceeded the configured burst policy for the p3 pool. The KV eviction caused extra recomputation per request which amplified latency and error rate.

Attached: incident_timeline_20270218.csv, service-traces-18.zip (excerpt).

Immediate mitigations we've already applied:
- Increased KV cache TTL for the customer prefix to avoid eviction for the next 48h.
- Emergency vertical capacity: added two additional nodes to the p3 pool for Lighthouse load.

Next steps (short):
- Produce RCA doc and recommended patch (by 2/21 EOD).
- Propose policy change to burst autoscaling thresholds (internal review).

I'll drop a detailed RCA and proposed capacity/quantization adjustments by EOD tomorrow.

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Executive readout & RCA summary for 2/18 Lighthouse impact

Eric / Lighthouse leadership —

Thank you for the call earlier. Below is the executive summary + commitments from Redwood. I appreciate your patience while we finished the technical write-up.

Executive summary (short):
- Root cause: KV cache eviction cascaded into extra model recomputation under an unexpected median->p95 sequence-length distribution shift. Our autoscaling burst policy for the p3 pool did not provision capacity quickly enough, producing latency >1s and increased 500 errors for ~38 minutes.
- Impact: traffic for Lighthouse's checkout inference route saw 7.8% 500 errors and ~3% client-visible timeouts; estimated customer conversions impacted for a small subset during the promo window.

Committed corrective actions and owners:
1) Short-term (now -> 72h): increase KV TTL for customer prefixes, leave elevated pool capacity for 72h. Owner: Marcus Lin. Due: 2027-02-24.
2) Medium-term (1–2 weeks): adjust burst autoscaler thresholds and add warm standby nodes for high-QPS customers. Owner: Grace O'Connor. Due: 2027-03-05.
3) Platform patch (2–4 weeks): reduce worst-case recomputation by adding an early-exit path for detected eviction patterns and improved sequence-length heuristics. Owner: SRE/Runtime team (Marcus/Grace). Due: 2027-03-15.
4) Commercial remediation: one month of service credit applied to Lighthouse commercial account; contract amendment to include higher burst SLA option if desired. Owner: Hannah Schmitt. Due: 2027-02-25.

Deliverables shared: RCA PDF (attached), incident timeline CSV, capacity adjustment plan (draft).

We propose a follow-up operational review on 2027-02-25 to validate mitigations and confirm timeline to closure. Please let us know availability.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
